correctness.rationale: Direct inversion of the unweighted Bergman two-kernel Gram matrix yields the displayed rational projection identity, confirmed symbolically and by 160 independent 60-digit Gram comparisons. The convex quadratic Q has an exact vertex and two sign-threshold polynomials with rigorously certified unique roots in the stated intervals. On its negative interval the strict logarithmic second-derivative inequality yields a unique maximizing angle, with a positive endpoint derivative excluding antipodal pairs. Coalescence is the two-dimensional value/first-derivative jet limit. All t in (0,1), all angular separations, ties, and nonattainment in the distinct-node class are addressed. The standalone check passed 179 assertions; numerics are not relied on as continuum proof.

originality.rationale: The 2021 Bergman paper gives general existence of best n-kernel approximants; the accessible 2022 paper treats still more general existence and not the fixed-radius two-node quadratic phase diagram. Direct title, alias, object and threshold searches, published-record semantic comparisons and accessible existing mathematical claims identified no implication that fixes either t0 or t1 or the coexistence/equality classification. The Hardy 2-kernel z-squared exact theorem uses the Szegő rather than Bergman kernel and does not imply this nonlinear weighted Gram statement. The circular regular-polygon Bergman kernel results require antipodal separation for two nodes and concern Fourier-mode aliasing/Gram spectra, whereas this work allows all angles and proves antipodal designs never optimize. A plausible 2021 full text was not accessible, so residual historical-priority risk is retained.

value.rationale: Fixing a sampling radius and optimizing two node placements is a natural, concrete rotationally constrained reproducing-kernel approximation problem. The theorem completely determines its angular optimum for every radius, uncovers an initially continuous split from a derivative jet followed by discontinuous coexistence and reentrant collision, and shows that antipodal regular placement never attains the optimum. Both critical radii are exact natural bifurcation points, not arbitrary numerical slices. This classifies attainment/nonattainment of a fundamental two-node approximation for a quadratic target, without relying on unsupported extrapolation to unequal radii.
